newsitem.title: USA: Mountasia sees Q3 loss, no immediate profit.
newsitem.headline: Mountasia sees Q3 loss, no immediate profit.

text.p: Mountasia Entertainment International Inc said Thursday it expects a third quarter loss and does not expect to return to sustainable profitability until benefits of a new business plan are realized.
The company said it expects to furnish details on the plan later this month.
It said the plan to restore profitability -- part of a plan to enhance shareholder value adopted by directors -- includes a search for a new chief executive.

Mountasia said it expects to report a third quarter loss of $2.0 million, or $0.14 per share, including a charge of $500,000, or $0.04 per share. for the early extinguishment of debt. This compares to a loss of $1.5 million, or $0.18 per share, in the year-ago period.

The company said the seasonal nature of its business, the fact that certain of its parks are presently performing below expectations, the time required to redevelop parks, and the fact that certain parks will need to be closed during redevelopment, makes profitability unlikely until the business plan benefits are realized.
It said the plan provides for redemption of its convertible debentures, sale of common stock at a premium to current market prices, and redemption of convertible debt not currently convertible.

Since completion of its $112 million recapitalization in August, Mountasia said, it has been involved in a review of its operations that identified a number of opportunities for improving operational results and achieving internal growth through the redevelopment, repositioning and expansion of existing parks.
The company said it intends to begin implementing these actions this winter and expects the steps to be completed in phases over the next several years.
Mountasia said it will also seek growth through acquisitions and the development of additional parks.

To do this, it has purchased interests it did not already own in three existing Mountasia parks, begun talks to buy the interest not owned in another park, accelerated the purchase of un-owned interests in an additional park, reacquired development rights previously sold, and agreed to buy a large existing family entertainment center in San Antonio, Texas.

While the search is being made for a permanent CEO, the company said, its new chairman, Robert Whitman, will serve as interim CEO. Whitman is co-CEO of the investor group that recapitalized the company in late August.
Mountasia also said Richard FitzPatrick, the group's CFO, has been elected interim CFO.
Under an agreement with the investor group, the funds to redeem convertible debt will be provided on terms more favorable than called for in the recapitalization agreement.

Non-voting preferred stock will be issues that will have a higher conversion price than specified under previous agreements. Also, the stock will have a liquidation preference equal to the amount received for issuance, be entitled to a 7.0 percent dividend before common dividends are paid, and will not be permitted to be converted into common stock unless shareholder approval is obtained.
The company said it expects to seek such approval at a special meeting of shareholders to be held in early 1997.
Mountasia said the investor group will offer other common stockholders $3.50 per share.
The offer is expected to start November 15 and expire on January 7.
It said no current directors intend to tender shares pursuant to the offer.
Until shareholder approval is obtained, shares purchased pursuant to the offer will effectively be non-voting.

The company said holders of convertible debt with a principal amount of about $15.7 million, which is not presently convertible, will be permitted to participate in the offer at a price which, in effect, assumes their conversion at the tender offer price.
Mountasia said it now has about 28.0 million common shares outstanding, of which the investor group owns 11.7 million.

Assuming the redemption of outstanding 10 percent, 9.0 percent and 9.1 percent debentures, and the expected issuance of 650,000 shares to settle claims against the company, the number of outstanding shares would increase by 7.7 million.

Issuance of these shares will result in another 6.4 million shares being issued to the investor group, without the payment of additional consideration, to protect the group from the dilutive effects of the 7.7 million share issuance.
-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
